name: Ghana Empire
summary: A West African empire of the Soninke people that grew rich from trans-Saharan gold trade. Arab writers called it the “land of gold”. Modern Ghana took its name.

knownFor.label: “Land of gold”
knownFor.note: Ghana controlled the trade of gold from the south for salt from the Sahara.

knownFor.label: Camel caravans
knownFor.note: Camels carried goods across the Sahara.

knownFor.label: Koumbi Saleh
knownFor.note: A twin-town capital described by al-Bakri.

location.value: Southern Mauritania and western Mali, between the Senegal and Niger rivers.

terrain.value: The Sahel, a belt of dry grassland between the Sahara and the savannah.

climate.value: Semi-arid, with a drying trend over the centuries.

resources.value: Access to the gold fields of Bambuk and Bure to the south; salt came from the Sahara.

disasters.value: Drought and desertification weakened farming and herding.

urbanisation.value: Koumbi Saleh had two towns, one for the king and one for Muslim merchants (described by al-Bakri in 1068).

migration.value: Muslim merchants from North Africa settled in the trading towns.

economicBase.value: Taxing the gold and salt trade, plus farming and herding.

tradeRoutes.value: Trans-Saharan caravan routes using camels, to Sijilmasa and North Africa.

wealth.value: No estimate is possible for this period; known as the “land of gold”.

moneyAndTax.value: Taxes on salt coming in and gold going out; the king kept all gold nuggets.

inequality.value: The king owned all gold nuggets.

governmentType.source: Wikipedia: Ghana Empire (checked 6 Nov 2026); Levtzion, Ancient Ghana and Mali (1973)

succession.value: Through the king’s sister’s son (matrilineal), according to al-Bakri.

institutions.value: Muslim scribes and officials served the king.

armyAndTech.value: A large army, reportedly 200,000 men, including archers.

majorWars.value: A conflict with the Almoravids (traditionally said to have conquered it in 1076, now doubted).

alliancesRivals.value: Rivals: the Almoravids and the Sosso.

scienceEducation.value: Islamic learning among merchants and officials.

openness.value: Welcomed Muslim traders while the king kept traditional religion.
openness.source: Wikipedia: Ghana Empire (checked 6 Nov 2026); Levtzion, Ancient Ghana and Mali (1973)

religion.value: African traditional religion, with Islam spreading from the 11th century.
religion.source: Wikipedia: Ghana Empire (checked 6 Nov 2026); Levtzion, Ancient Ghana and Mali (1973)

languageWriting.value: Soninke and other Mande languages; Arabic used by Muslim scribes.
languageWriting.source: Wikipedia: Ghana Empire (checked 6 Nov 2026); Levtzion, Ancient Ghana and Mali (1973)

artsArchitecture.value: Stone houses and mosques at Koumbi Saleh.

socialStructure.value: Royal clan, merchants, farmers and slaves.

neighbours.value: The Sosso, Mali, the Almoravids and Takrur.
neighbours.source: Wikipedia: Ghana Empire (checked 6 Nov 2026); Levtzion, Ancient Ghana and Mali (1973)

ideasReligions.source: Wikipedia: Ghana Empire (checked 6 Nov 2026); Levtzion, Ancient Ghana and Mali (1973)

riseSignals.source: Wikipedia: Ghana Empire (checked 6 Nov 2026); Levtzion, Ancient Ghana and Mali (1973)

declineSignals.value: Loss of trade, drought and the rise of rivals.
declineSignals.source: Wikipedia: Ghana Empire (checked 6 Nov 2026); Levtzion, Ancient Ghana and Mali (1973)

outcome.value: Became a vassal of the Mali Empire in the 13th century.

sources.value: Arabic writers (al-Bakri, al-Idrisi). Checked against Wikipedia (“Ghana Empire”).

overallCertainty.value: Low to medium. Origins are uncertain.
